articles.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak

events.summary: Government records indicate over 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak to date. Total recorded infections have surpassed 10,000 cases.
events.why: A 50% mortality rate across 10,000 cases represents a catastrophic public health emergency with severe epidemic transmission risks.

articles.title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

events.summary: Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has launched a new rebel movement.
events.why: A former head of state forming an armed insurgency risks reigniting large-scale armed conflict and regional instability in DR Congo.

articles.title: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza

events.summary: The UN human rights office reported that Israeli military operations are confining Palestinians to shrinking areas while destroying infrastructure and targeting displacement sites. OHCHR warned of potential ethnic cleansing amidst the escalating displacement crisis.
events.why: Systematic destruction and severe civilian compression threaten permanent demographic displacement and mass casualties.

articles.title: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes

events.summary: Three decades of UN political missions in Somalia are ending, marking a key transition for the Horn of Africa country. UN leadership described the engagement as an era of persistence, partnership, and adaptation.
events.why: The complete withdrawal of a 30-year UN political framework significantly shifts governance and security responsibilities to Somalia's sovereign institutions.

articles.title: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks

events.summary: More than 28 million people in the DRC face food shortages, with hunger levels projected to rise further due to conflict, Ebola, and climate shocks. The warning was published by the global food monitor IPC.
events.why: Tens of millions face severe malnutrition driven by compounding crises of disease, warfare, and extreme weather.

articles.title: Health authorities probe two suspected Ebola cases in northeast Nigeria

events.summary: Health authorities in northeast Nigeria are investigating two suspected Ebola cases. The individuals have been isolated while contact tracing and laboratory tests are conducted.
events.why: A potential outbreak of Ebola carries severe public health and epidemic containment risks across the region.

articles.title: India's opposition set to hold mega rally seeking election chief's resignation

events.summary: India's opposition is preparing a major rally demanding the election chief's resignation amid disputes over voter roll revisions. Critics fear the revision process could disenfranchise 130 million registered voters.
events.why: Disenfranchisement risks on this scale directly challenge democratic legitimacy in the world's most populous nation.

articles.title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack

events.summary: Suspected North Korean hackers are the primary suspects in a record-breaking cyber heist targeting cryptocurrency exchange Binance.
events.why: Major state-sponsored cyber operations targeting global financial platforms provide illicit revenue and demonstrate growing systemic digital vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue

events.summary: Countries have reached a global agreement to halt nature decline, though funding remains unresolved. The negotiations aimed to get international biodiversity efforts back on track.
events.why: Global biodiversity agreements govern worldwide conservation policy and impact ecosystem survival, though effectiveness hinges on resolving funding shortfalls.

articles.title: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many

events.summary: Fighting in Yemen has displaced more than 280,000 individuals, according to the UN refugee agency. The insecurity has rendered it too dangerous for many vulnerable people to receive lifesaving relief.
events.why: Severe security threats prevent critical aid delivery to hundreds of thousands of displaced individuals facing acute crisis.

articles.title: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official

events.summary: Despite introducing internal advancements such as mobile banking, smartphones, and new factories, the DPRK has left its population more isolated from the outside world than ever. This assessment was issued by a UN human rights official.
events.why: Deepening isolation directly compounds state control and human rights violations over an entire national population.

articles.title: He questioned Thailand's monarchy dressed as Harry Potter. Now he's in jail for 34 years

events.summary: A Thai activist was sentenced to 34 years in prison after questioning the monarchy during a protest. Thailand has prosecuted 294 individuals under its lèse majesté law since 2020, issuing sentences up to 50 years.
events.why: The rigorous enforcement of harsh lèse-majesté laws represents a systematic suppression of political speech and civil liberties across Thailand.

articles.title: Turkiye’s Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks

events.summary: Turkish President Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to halt Black Sea attacks during a meeting with President Zelenskyy in Istanbul. Both leaders agreed to collaborate on establishing a new Black Sea grain corridor.
events.why: Restoring a Black Sea grain corridor directly impacts global food security and maritime navigation in a major conflict zone.

articles.title: At least four Palestinians killed in Gaza as Israeli attacks continue

events.summary: Israeli attacks in Gaza, including the shelling of the Nuseirat refugee camp, have killed at least four Palestinians.
events.why: It documents ongoing casualties and military strikes within a civilian refugee area.

articles.title: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World Cities Day

events.summary: Over 300,000 individuals remain internally displaced in Lebanon since early March, according to the UN's aid coordination office. OCHA warned that the ongoing humanitarian crisis is far from over.
events.why: Large-scale displacement exacerbates Lebanon's ongoing socioeconomic collapse and regional stability.

articles.title: They strangled us, says founder of Russian newspaper shut under pressure from authorities

events.summary: Prominent independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta has shut down under pressure from authorities. The founder stated that official pressure effectively strangled the three-decade-old publication.
events.why: The closure of Russia's most prominent independent news outlet marks a major contraction in domestic press freedom.

articles.title: The fight to save Canadian town threatened by Trump's tariffs

events.summary: A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec has closed indefinitely after the United States imposed 50% tariffs on its products. The closure has left hundreds of workers unemployed.
events.why: Targeted trade tariffs can directly eliminate primary employers and destabilize local single-industry economies.

articles.title: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody

events.summary: The UN human rights chief has demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni UN staff member held in Houthi custody for over two years. The victim's family was notified only weeks after his death occurred.
events.why: The custodial death of international personnel highlights worsening threats to diplomatic immunity and aid operations in Houthi-held Yemen.

articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Who will form Israel’s next government?

events.summary: Netanyahu and Eisenkot are competing to assemble a governing coalition within Israel's Knesset.
events.why: The outcome determines the leadership and political direction of Israel's national government.

articles.title: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election

events.summary: A recent train disaster has added to political crises facing Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez just weeks before a snap election. The events complicate his administration's chances for re-election.
events.why: Major infrastructure failures near national elections can decisively swing voting outcomes and reshape government leadership.

articles.title: How vulnerable are cryptocurrency platforms?

events.summary: Hackers have targeted Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
events.why: Security threats to the largest digital asset exchange could affect the financial assets of millions of global users.

articles.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
Evacuees of Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with families
Ukraine news: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Kyiv-controlled territory
Ukraine: Oleshky residents evacuate war-ravaged city
Oleshky evacuees reunite with families after truce allows crossing back into Ukraine

events.summary: Evacuated residents from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrived at the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus via buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire. They have now reached Kyiv-controlled territory to reunite with families.
events.why: It marks a successful humanitarian corridor facilitating civilian evacuation across conflict lines during an active war.

articles.title: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue

events.summary: The UN's top humanitarian official noted that each day the Oleshky ceasefire holds provides hope for civilians, though attacks on aid vehicles persist. The official emphasized that residents wishing to leave must be permitted safe and voluntary passage.
events.why: Fragile local ceasefires determine civilian survival and the viability of international humanitarian operations under ongoing fire.

articles.title: Palestinians ‘Stealing their own olives’

events.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank have turned the olive harvest into a deadly activity for Palestinians.
events.why: It reflects ongoing violence and territorial tensions impacting the safety and livelihoods of local residents in the West Bank.
